message.content:
This is a /simplify review (code QUALITY, not correctness bugs) of uncommitted changes in /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim. Theme: a new C++ driver (F6 "phase-plan executor") was added, and the "vsim -> QEMU2 handback" leg was removed repo-wide (mostly deletions).

YOUR ANGLE: EFFICIENCY. Flag wasted work the new code introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O, independent operations run sequentially, blocking work on hot/startup paths. Name the cheaper alternative. (This is a CLI orchestrator, not a hot loop -- so weight findings by whether they actually matter; a per-step map build is fine, a redundant subprocess spawn is not.)

SCOPE (review only these CODE files; IGNORE all *.md docs):
NEW code -- Read the whole files:
  driver/argv.cpp, driver/argv.hpp, driver/plan.hpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
  driver/run_plan.hpp, driver/plan_test.cpp, driver/plan_itest.cpp,
  driver/shm.cpp, driver/shm.hpp, driver/state.hpp, driver/infra_test.cpp
MODIFIED -- `git diff HEAD -- <file>`:
  driver/engine_registry.cpp, driver/process.cpp, driver/process.hpp
  tools/orchestrator/{spawn.py,runner.py,main.py}
  tests/e2e.sh, scripts/run_e2e.sh

Look especially for:
- run_plan.cpp: is `plan_argvs` re-finding the engine descriptor per step (linear scan) when it could resolve once? Is the state file read back redundantly? Does run_plan call discover_engines or re-stat anything per step?
- plan_itest.cpp: any redundant discover_engines / repeated work?
- engine_registry.cpp: the qemu template build -- any per-call rebuild that could be static?
- process.cpp: the spawn/poll loop -- any busy-wait or redundant syscall the F5 edit added?
- e2e.sh / run_e2e.sh: did the 2-phase edit leave a now-redundant mktemp / trap / process the harness no longer needs?

The orchestrator/vsim changes are mostly DELETIONS (which REMOVE work -- good) -- only flag NEW waste.

First read the scope files, then report. Each finding: `file:line` + one-line summary + the cheaper alternative + whether it actually matters here. If clean, say so. Do NOT report correctness bugs. Do NOT touch docs.

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
31	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
32	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
33	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
34	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
35	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
36	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
37	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
38	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
39	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
40	
41	struct PlanOptions {
42	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
43	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
44	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
45	};
46	
47	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
48	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
49	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
50	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
51	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
52	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
53	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
54	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
55	
56	}  // namespace andes_sim
57	
58	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
59

1	// Placeholder substitution for engine invoke templates -- the template-driven
2	// port of orchestrator/spawn.py (minus QEMU2). spawn.py hand-built each argv in
3	// Python; here the argv *shape* lives in each engine's `invoke` template (from
4	// `--describe`, see docs/engine_interface.md) and build_argv fills the
5	// {placeholders} from a context map. The framework thus keeps zero per-engine
6	// argv code: a new engine ships its own template.
7	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
8	#define ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
9	
10	#include <map>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <vector>
13	
14	namespace andes_sim {
15	
16	// Substitute every "{key}" in `tmpl`'s args with `ctx.at(key)`. A key may
17	// appear anywhere in an arg (so "mem-path={mmap},size={mmap_size}" expands in
18	// one arg) and more than once. Recognised keys come from `ctx`; a "{key}" with
19	// no matching ctx entry is an error (returns {} and sets `err`). On success
20	// `err` is cleared and the fully-resolved argv is returned.
21	std::vector<std::string> build_argv(const std::vector<std::string>& tmpl,
22	                                    const std::map<std::string, std::string>& ctx,
23	                                    std::string& err);
24	
25	}  // namespace andes_sim
26	
27	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
28

1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andes-sim -- a C++ port of tools/hsim_shm.py.
2	//
3	// One rule: the caller asks for `size` bytes; we honor HSIM_MMAP_DIR (else
4	// /dev/shm), statvfs-check free space, allocate a sparse file with
5	// mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line. No fallback chain, no
6	// filesystem-type probing. (The HSIM_MMAP_DIR name and "[hsim mmap]" status
7	// line stay verbatim with the Python golden until the F14 rename.)
8	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <string>
12	
13	namespace andes_sim {
14	
15	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
16	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
17	// to the argparse-style message. Mirrors hsim_shm.parse_size (fractional values
18	// truncate, like Python int(float(num) * mult)).
19	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
20	
21	// Resolve the pinned mmap directory (HSIM_MMAP_DIR if set, else /dev/shm) and
22	// validate it can hold size + 256 MiB. Returns the directory on success; on
23	// failure returns "" and sets `err`. Mirrors hsim_shm.select_mmap_dir.
24	std::string select_mmap_dir(long long size, std::string& err);
25	
26	// Allocate a sparse mmap file of `size` bytes in the pinned dir (mkstemp +
27	// truncate), print one "[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)" line, and
28	// return its path. On failure returns "" and sets `err`. Caller owns the file's
29	// lifetime (unlink when done). Mirrors hsim_shm.allocate.
30	std::string allocate(long long size, std::string& err,
31	                     const std::string& prefix = "hsim-shm.");
32	
33	}  // namespace andes_sim
34	
35	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's milmb ROI markers via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./hsim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
21	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
22	#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
23	#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
24	#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
25	#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
26	#                              pair from the drained state file.
27	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
28	
29	set -euo pipefail
30	
31	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
32	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
33	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
34	
35	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
36	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
37	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"
38	
39	hybrid_resolve_paths
40	
41	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
42	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
43	
44	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
45	  csr) ;;
46	  pc)
47	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
48	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
49	      exit 77
50	    fi
51	    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
52	    # $VSIM_ELF). ./hsim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
53	    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
54	    # from the fixture's milmb ROI markers via objdump, so pc mode needs no
55	    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
56	    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
57	    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
58	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
59	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
60	      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
61	         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
62	        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
63	        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
64	        export ROI_START ROI_END
65	      fi
66	    fi
67	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
68	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
69	    ;;
70	  *)
71	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
72	    exit 1
73	    ;;
74	esac
75	
76	# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
77	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
78	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
79	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
80	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
81	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
82	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
83	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
84	
85	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
86	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
87	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
88	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
89	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
90	fi
91	
92	# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
93	VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
94	if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
95	  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
96	fi
97	
98	# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
99	# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
100	# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
101	VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
102	if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
103	  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
104	  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
105	    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
106	  fi
107	fi
108	
109	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
110	set +e
111	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
112	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
113	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
114	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
115	  -nographic \
116	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
117	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
118	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
119	QEMU1_RC=$?
120	set -e
121	
122	if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
123	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
124	  exit 1
125	fi
126	
127	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
128	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
129	  exit 1
130	fi
131	
132	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
133	set +e
134	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
135	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
136	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
137	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
138	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
139	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
140	  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
141	  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
142	  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
143	VSIM_RC=$?
144	set -e
145	
146	# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
147	# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
148	# drained cleanly.
149	if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
150	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
151	  echo "--- sim log ---"
152	  cat "$SIM_LOG"
153	  exit 1
154	fi
155	
156	# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
157	# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
158	# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
159	# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
160	# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
161	if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
162	  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
163	  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
164	  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
165	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
166	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
167	  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
168	  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
169	  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
170	  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
171	  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
172	  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
173	    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
174	    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
175	    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
176	  fi
177	  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
178	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
179	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
180	    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
181	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
182	      exit 1
183	    fi
184	    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
185	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
186	      exit 1
187	    fi
188	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
189	  fi
190	fi
191	
192	echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"
193

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
3	# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
4	# workspace.
5	#
6	# Env overrides:
7	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
8	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
9	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
10	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
11	#   MODE         csr | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
12	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
13	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
14	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
15	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
16	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
17	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
18	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
19	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
20	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
21	
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
25	VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
26	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
27	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
28	
29	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
30	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
31	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
32	  VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
33	fi
34	
35	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
37	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
38	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
39	
40	require() {
41	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
42	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
43	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"

45	  fi
46	}

48	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
49	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

52	
53	REQUIRED_ELFS=(
54	  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
55	  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
56	  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs

62	need_build=0

69	fi
70	
71	# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
72	# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
73	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
74	# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
75	RT_TESTS=(
76	  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
77	  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
78	  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
79	  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
80	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
81	  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
82	  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
83	  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
84	  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"

89	  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
90	  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
91	  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"

94	
95	NEG_TESTS=(

108	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
109	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
110	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
111	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
112	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
113	    fi
114	  fi
115	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
116	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
117	}
118	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
119	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
120	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
121	
122	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
123	
124	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
125	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
126	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
127	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
128	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
129	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
130	
131	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
132	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
133	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
134	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
135	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
136	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
137	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
138	run_one() {
139	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
140	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
141	  local start end elapsed status rc
142	  start=$(date +%s)
143	  set +e
144	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
145	  rc=$?
146	  set -e
147	  end=$(date +%s)
148	  elapsed=$((end - start))
149	  case $rc in
150	    0)  status=PASS ;;
151	    77) status=SKIP ;;
152	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
153	  esac
154	  (
155	    flock 9
156	    case "$status" in
157	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
158	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
159	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
160	    esac
161	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
162	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
163	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
164	}
165	
166	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
167	# matters: csr-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
168	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
169	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
170	for tm in csr pc; do
171	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
172	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
173	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
174	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
175	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
176	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*csr.*'.
177	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
178	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
179	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
180	  done
181	done
182	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
183	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
184	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
185	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
186	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
187	done
188	
189	TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
190	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
191	
192	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
193	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
194	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
195	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
196	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
197	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
198	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
199	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
200	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
201	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
202	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
203	  printf '.\n' >&8
204	done
205	
206	i=0
207	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
208	  i=$((i+1))
209	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
210	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
211	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
212	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
213	  read -r -u 8 _tok
214	  (
215	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
216	    printf '.\n' >&8
217	  ) &
218	done
219	wait
220	exec 8>&-
221	
222	declare -A MODE_PASS=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
223	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
224	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
225	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
226	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
227	  case "$r_status" in
228	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
229	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
230	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
231	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
232	  esac
233	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
234	
235	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
236	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
237	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
238	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
239	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
240	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
241	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
242	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
243	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
244	    echo
245	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
246	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
247	  fi
248	done
249	
250	echo
251	csr_p=${MODE_PASS[csr]} csr_f=${MODE_FAIL[csr]} csr_s=${MODE_SKIP[csr]}
252	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
253	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
254	total_pass=$((csr_p + pc_p + neg_p))
255	total_fail=$((csr_f + pc_f + neg_f))
256	total_skip=$((csr_s + pc_s + neg_s))
257	step "summary: csr ${csr_p}p/${csr_f}f/${csr_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
258	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
259	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
260	  exit 1
261	fi
262

Read complete. Here are the efficiency findings, weighted by whether they actually matter for this CLI orchestrator.

## Verdict: clean on the efficiency axis. No finding that actually matters.

The new code introduces no redundant subprocess spawn, no repeated I/O, no busy-wait, and no blocking work that could be avoided. The plan legs are inherently sequential (leg N+1 resumes from leg N's drain), so there is no missed parallelism. Below are the items you flagged to check, each with a verdict.

### Items checked, all non-issues

**`run_plan.cpp:25-30,50` -- `find_engine` linear scan per step.** Yes, it re-scans `engines` for every step instead of resolving once into a map. Cheaper: build a `map<id, const EngineDescriptor*>` once before the loop. Does NOT matter: N_engines is ~2-4 and N_steps is ~2; a map would be over-engineering for this size. Leave as-is.

**`run_plan.cpp:63` + `run_plan.cpp:150` -- `state_path(wd, i)` computed twice.** `plan_argvs` builds the path into the argv (line 63), then the spawn loop recomputes the identical string to read it back (line 150). Cheaper: have `plan_argvs` return the state paths alongside the argvs, or read them from a stored vector. Does NOT matter: it is a sub-100-byte string concat, not I/O, run once per leg.

**`state.hpp:24-61` -- `read_state_file` reads the whole `hybrid_state_v1` (~3.4 KB) for just `mcycle`/`minstret`.** Not wasteful: it is a single `fread` of a tiny file, and the full read is needed anyway to validate magic/version. The `fseek/ftell/rewind` size check is one extra seek pair but negligible. Correct as written.

**`engine_registry.cpp:40-47` -- `builtin_qemu()` rebuilds the ~15-string invoke template on every call.** Could be `static const`. Does NOT matter: `builtin_qemu()` is called once per `discover_engines()`, which is a once-per-process startup path, not a loop. Static would save nothing observable.

**`process.cpp` (F5 edit) -- the diff is a pure refactor.** The F5 change only extracted the shared fork/exec/wait body into `spawn_inherit` (backing both `run_inherit` and the new `exec_passthrough`); it removes duplication and adds no waste. The `run_process` poll loop (lines 104-134) is unchanged by this diff and is event-driven (`poll` blocks on the fd/timeout), not a busy-wait. It calls `now_ms()` twice per iteration (lines 105, 129), but that is a vDSO `clock_gettime`, not a real syscall, and is pre-existing. Nothing new.

**`plan_itest.cpp:31` -- `discover_engines()` called exactly once**, then `disc.engines` is reused for the vsim scan and passed to `run_plan`. No redundant discovery, no re-stat per step. `run_plan` takes `engines` as a parameter and never re-discovers. Clean.

### Harness deletions left nothing redundant

**`tests/e2e.sh`** -- the QEMU2 block removal also removed its `ORCH_LOG=$(mktemp)` and the second `trap '...ORCH_LOG' EXIT` together. The surviving trap at `tests/e2e.sh:82` still cleans the 4 live temp files (`SHARED_MEM`, `STATE_QEMU`, `STATE_VSIM`, `SIM_LOG`). No orphaned mktemp, no leak, no redundant trap.

**`scripts/run_e2e.sh`** -- diff is comment-only plus dropping the now-dead `EXPECT_RC=3`. The FIFO job pool, `LOG_DIR` mktemp, and `SEM_FIFO` are pre-existing and untouched. Clean.

**`tools/orchestrator/{spawn,runner,main}.py`** -- pure deletions of the QEMU2 path (removes work). No new waste introduced.
